name: Features replace use cases
description: Lastro says feature wherever it said use case, in files, ids, CLI, SDKs, prompts, UIs and docs; features are broader and functionality-oriented, an intent may change one or more features, and this repository migrates once with no backward compatibility.
prose:
# Features replace use cases

The application is its list of features. "Feature" is the word the business already uses for what a product does
for its users, so Lastro uses it everywhere it said "use case": in the files, the ids, the CLI, the SDKs' public
API, the prompts, the review app, the plugin, the board, the receipt and the docs. A feature has the same fields, the
same history and the same proofs a use case had, and every rule that held for use cases holds for features.

## What a feature is

A feature is broader than a use case and is written around the functionality itself: what the product lets its users
do, in the business's words, with the complete behavior of that functionality as the code implements it. The
extraction and survey prompts write and group features that way.

An intent is the intention to change the application: it modifies one or more existing features, adds a new one or
removes one. A modify intent names every feature it changes, and each of those features' new description combines all
the intents that change it.

## Files and ids

Each feature lives in `.lastro/features/<id>-<slug>.json` and is numbered F-001, F-002... with the next free
number, never reused. Proofs derived straight from a feature are numbered inside it (F-003.PF-01); proofs that came
from a proposal keep their proposal id. A proof file names its feature in a `feature` field. A proposal's intents
name the features they add, modify or remove, and its baseline is the hash over the canonical features.

This repository's own use cases are migrated once, as part of this change: each use case becomes the feature with
the same number (UC-003 becomes F-003), every proof and proposal that names it is rewritten with the new id, and
`.lastro/usecases/` is removed. Lastro keeps no reader for the old layout and no old names: the framework has no
users yet.

## Commands and API

`lastro derive --features`, `lastro prove --features` and every other option that took use cases take features;
`--usecases` no longer exists. In the TypeScript, Go and .NET SDKs every public type, function and field that said
use case says feature, with no aliases. The extraction and derivation prompts and their schemas say feature, and
the .NET and Go prompts are generated from the TypeScript ones as before.

## What people see

The review app, the plugin's review, the progress board and the receipt say feature and show F- ids. The docs
explain features as what the product does for its users, in the user's words, and nothing in the repository says use
case any more.

useCases.name: Extract intents from prose
useCases.before: propose(prose, { submittedBy }) creates the next proposal file in .lastro/proposals/ with status open and sends the prose and the current use cases to an LLM through an AskJson transport with a fixed system prompt and JSON Schema (step "extract"). The answer lists intents, each the addition, removal or change of exactly one use case: id (P-n.I-nn), slug, name, a natural-language description of the change, change (add, modify or remove), the use case (an existing id, or a newly reserved id and slug for an add), a provability (formal, empirical, beyond-proof), a beyondProofReason ("none" or one of the five reasons) and a verbatim quote, and replaces: the existing proofs of that use case the new behavior contradicts, each with a reason (extraction receives every touched use case with its proofs in readable notation; for a remove the SDK lists every proof of the use case itself); one resulting use case per touched use case with its name and, for add and modify, the complete new description (after), all its intents combined, and the intents that produce it; decisions that reference intents by zero-based index; and notPromised items. The SDK fills each modify and remove with the use case's current description (before); the LLM never supplies it. The proposal (lastro: proposal/v1) records the baseline (sha256 over the canonical use cases without their proofs), the submitter, every intent proposed with no approvals, decisions D1, D2... with origin extraction, and the review policy. Intents have no kind. Without an LLM transport or a custom extractor, propose() throws.
useCases.after: propose(prose, { submittedBy }) creates the next proposal file in .lastro/proposals/ with status open and sends the prose and the current features to an LLM through an AskJson transport with a fixed system prompt and JSON Schema (step "extract"). The answer lists intents, each the addition, removal or change of exactly one feature: id (P-n.I-nn), slug, name, a natural-language description of the change, change (add, modify or remove), the feature (an existing id, or a newly reserved id and slug for an add), a provability (formal, empirical, beyond-proof), a beyondProofReason ("none" or one of the five reasons) and a verbatim quote, and replaces: the existing proofs of that feature the new behavior contradicts, each with a reason (extraction receives every touched feature with its proofs in readable notation; for a remove the SDK lists every proof of the feature itself); one resulting feature per touched feature with its name and, for add and modify, the complete new description (after), all its intents combined, and the intents that produce it; decisions that reference intents by zero-based index; and notPromised items. The SDK fills each modify and remove with the feature's current description (before); the LLM never supplies it. The proposal (lastro: proposal/v1) records the baseline (sha256 over the canonical features without their proofs), the submitter, every intent proposed with no approvals, decisions D1, D2... with origin extraction, and the review policy. Intents have no kind. Without an LLM transport or a custom extractor, propose() throws. Features are written and grouped at the level of a functionality: what the product lets its users do, in the business's words, with its complete behavior. An intent modifies one or more existing features, adds a new one or removes one; a modify intent names every feature it changes, and each changed feature's after combines all the intents that change it.

useCases.name: Anchor every intent to the prose
useCases.before: Each intent stores its quote with start and end offsets into the prose (the intent map). The quote is searched verbatim first, then ignoring case and runs of whitespace from a word boundary. The whole extraction is rejected with an ArtifactError listing every problem if any quote is not found; a beyond-proof intent has no reason or a reason is unknown; a decision has fewer than two options, a recommended index out of range or an unknown intent; a modify or remove names a use case that does not exist; an add does not reserve a new id and a new kebab-case slug; an add or modify has no after; a touched use case does not have exactly one resulting use case listing at least one intent; or an intent replaces a proof that does not exist or belongs to another use case.
useCases.after: Each intent stores its quote with start and end offsets into the prose (the intent map). The quote is searched verbatim first, then ignoring case and runs of whitespace from a word boundary. The whole extraction is rejected with an ArtifactError listing every problem if any quote is not found; a beyond-proof intent has no reason or a reason is unknown; a decision has fewer than two options, a recommended index out of range or an unknown intent; a modify or remove names a feature that does not exist; an add does not reserve a new id and a new kebab-case slug; an add or modify has no after; a touched feature does not have exactly one resulting feature listing at least one intent; or an intent replaces a proof that does not exist or belongs to another feature.

useCases.name: Turn ambiguity into decision cards
useCases.before: The extraction prompt tells the model not to guess when the prose is ambiguous and to return a decision instead: one question, two to four options each with a consequence, and the index of the recommended option, preferably about cases the author has not considered. Each becomes a decision card tied to the intents it concerns. Intents on one use case whose change kinds do not fit together (an add or a remove mixed with a modify, or a remove combined with anything) and two intents that contradict each other on one use case also come back as decisions. A card with origin extraction records the chosen option when answered and creates no intent.
useCases.after: The extraction prompt tells the model not to guess when the prose is ambiguous and to return a decision instead: one question, two to four options each with a consequence, and the index of the recommended option, preferably about cases the author has not considered. Each becomes a decision card tied to the intents it concerns. Intents on one feature whose change kinds do not fit together (an add or a remove mixed with a modify, or a remove combined with anything) and two intents that contradict each other on one feature also come back as decisions. A card with origin extraction records the chosen option when answered and creates no intent.

useCases.name: Review intents
useCases.before: review(proposal, reviewer) returns a chainable review on a copy of the proposal (an approved proposal is reopened first). approve(ids) marks intents approved (an amended intent stays amended) and adds the reviewer to approvals once; approveAll() approves every intent that is not rejected; reject(id, note) sets status rejected, records the note with the reviewer's name and clears approvals; amend(id, description, patch?, note?) keeps the first original description, rewrites the description (optionally provability or beyond-proof reason), sets status amended and resets approvals to the amender alone. Review shows each intent with the proofs it replaces, their formal statements and the reasons; approving the intent accepts that those proofs will be replaced by proofs of the new behavior, and a reviewer who disagrees with the list amends the intent. A rejected intent drops out of its use case, replaces nothing and never reaches derivation or implementation. Rejecting or amending an intent marks its use case's after stale: the reviewer either writes the new after by hand (rewriteAfter(useCase, text)) or has the LLM recombine it from the remaining intents (recombine(useCase, instructions?), part of the extract step, through the same LLM or handoff), and that use case's intents need review again. done() returns the new proposal; unknown ids throw.
useCases.after: review(proposal, reviewer) returns a chainable review on a copy of the proposal (an approved proposal is reopened first). approve(ids) marks intents approved (an amended intent stays amended) and adds the reviewer to approvals once; approveAll() approves every intent that is not rejected; reject(id, note) sets status rejected, records the note with the reviewer's name and clears approvals; amend(id, description, patch?, note?) keeps the first original description, rewrites the description (optionally provability or beyond-proof reason), sets status amended and resets approvals to the amender alone. Review shows each intent with the proofs it replaces, their formal statements and the reasons; approving the intent accepts that those proofs will be replaced by proofs of the new behavior, and a reviewer who disagrees with the list amends the intent. A rejected intent drops out of its feature, replaces nothing and never reaches derivation or implementation. Rejecting or amending an intent marks its feature's after stale: the reviewer either writes the new after by hand (rewriteAfter(feature, text)) or has the LLM recombine it from the remaining intents (recombine(feature, instructions?), part of the extract step, through the same LLM or handoff), and that feature's intents need review again. done() returns the new proposal; unknown ids throw.

useCases.name: Approve the reviewed intents
useCases.before: approve() refuses with every pending item while anything is pending; a proposal is approved when every intent is approved, amended or rejected and every decision and thread is resolved. Otherwise it returns an approved copy with status approved whose hash = sha256 over canonical JSON (keys sorted, undefined dropped) of the proposal without its hash, which binds the baseline: if the use cases changed since extraction, the approval is stale and the prose must be extracted again. Only an approved proposal can be derived, so only approved and amended intents generate proofs and reach whoever implements the change; they and the resulting use cases are the implementer's brief. An approved proposal cannot be reviewed; reopen() returns a copy without the hash, which must be approved again. isApproved() recomputes the hash, so any edit after approval is detected, and derive and apply reject a proposal that is not approved or was modified after approval.
useCases.after: approve() refuses with every pending item while anything is pending; a proposal is approved when every intent is approved, amended or rejected and every decision and thread is resolved. Otherwise it returns an approved copy with status approved whose hash = sha256 over canonical JSON (keys sorted, undefined dropped) of the proposal without its hash, which binds the baseline: if the features changed since extraction, the approval is stale and the prose must be extracted again. Only an approved proposal can be derived, so only approved and amended intents generate proofs and reach whoever implements the change; they and the resulting features are the implementer's brief. An approved proposal cannot be reviewed; reopen() returns a copy without the hash, which must be approved again. isApproved() recomputes the hash, so any edit after approval is detected, and derive and apply reject a proposal that is not approved or was modified after approval.

useCases.name: Keep the review when the prose changes
useCases.before: Extracting a proposal's edited prose again carries the previous review over. A new intent with the same change, use case and description, ignoring case and whitespace, as a previously reviewed (non-proposed) intent takes its status, approvals, review note and original description. If instead the AI repeats the original reading of an amended intent for the same use case and quote, the amendment is reapplied with its approvals. Everything else stays proposed, so intents that changed lose their approvals. Decisions with the same question keep their answer when the option still exists, threads are kept, and the policy is kept. Decisions raised by the consistency check, and their intents, are not carried.
useCases.after: Extracting a proposal's edited prose again carries the previous review over. A new intent with the same change, feature and description, ignoring case and whitespace, as a previously reviewed (non-proposed) intent takes its status, approvals, review note and original description. If instead the AI repeats the original reading of an amended intent for the same feature and quote, the amendment is reapplied with its approvals. Everything else stays proposed, so intents that changed lose their approvals. Decisions with the same question keep their answer when the option still exists, threads are kept, and the policy is kept. Decisions raised by the consistency check, and their intents, are not carried.

useCases.name: Derive the proof plan
useCases.before: derive(proposal) requires an approved proposal and asks the LLM (step "derive") with the models declared in .lastro/config.json, each touched use case's before and after with its approved and amended intents, the existing proofs of those use cases, each decision's question and answer (the chosen or else the recommended option) and notPromised. It writes pending proofs into the proposal, numbered P-n.PF-nn: each has a slug, name and description, the intent and use case it checks, the model and subject it runs against, and a check that is either a clause (requires and ensures in LSL, assumptions used) or a scenario (concrete input and an LSL expect); plus assumptions and beyondProof items. Every remove intent gets a proof, written from the use case's before, that the old behavior no longer happens; when the model cannot express it, derivation returns a decision for the reviewer and the proposal cannot be applied while it is open. Derivation never retires a proof: the proposal's supersedes is the union of replaces over the approved and amended intents, each new proof that takes the place of one lists it, and an existing proof the approved behavior breaks that no approved intent replaces comes back as a decision that sends the intent back to review with the proof added to its replaces. Every expression is parsed and validated. The proposal moves to proving. Without an LLM transport or a custom deriver, derive() throws.
useCases.after: derive(proposal) requires an approved proposal and asks the LLM (step "derive") with the models declared in .lastro/config.json, each touched feature's before and after with its approved and amended intents, the existing proofs of those features, each decision's question and answer (the chosen or else the recommended option) and notPromised. It writes pending proofs into the proposal, numbered P-n.PF-nn: each has a slug, name and description, the intent and feature it checks, the model and subject it runs against, and a check that is either a clause (requires and ensures in LSL, assumptions used) or a scenario (concrete input and an LSL expect); plus assumptions and beyondProof items. Every remove intent gets a proof, written from the feature's before, that the old behavior no longer happens; when the model cannot express it, derivation returns a decision for the reviewer and the proposal cannot be applied while it is open. Derivation never retires a proof: the proposal's supersedes is the union of replaces over the approved and amended intents, each new proof that takes the place of one lists it, and an existing proof the approved behavior breaks that no approved intent replaces comes back as a decision that sends the intent back to review with the proof added to its replaces. Every expression is parsed and validated. The proposal moves to proving. Without an LLM transport or a custom deriver, derive() throws.

useCases.name: Render a receipt
useCases.before: The receipt is Markdown for a pull request, written next to the proposal: the overall result and counts per verdict; the proposal and plan hashes; the Rust check with coverage, table digest and whether verdicts agree; the use-case diff, with each use case added, modified (before and after) or removed with the intents behind it, each replaced proof next to the proofs that take its place, each superseded proof that still passes, each regression and, after apply, the new baseline hash; a table of intents with verdict, evidence, confidence and what backs each; notes; each proof with verdict, evidence, method (exhaustive, samples with failure bound, traces), mutants killed, formal statement, counterexample, violating trace and notes; trusted pieces; where proof stops; not promised; and pending contradictions.

useCases.name: Run the pipeline from a CLI
useCases.before: The CLIs (lastro in TypeScript and .NET, lastro-go in Go) run init --model model.json [--approvals N], propose <prose-file> [--section <heading>] [--as <submitter>], status [<proposal>], review <proposal> --as <name> approve|approve-all|amend|reject|answer|comment|resolve, derive <proposal>, prove <proposal>, feedback <proposal>, apply <proposal> and regress. Each prints one JSON object and keeps state in a workspace directory (default .lastro, --dir to change): config.json (models, subjects and the review block), usecases/, proposals/ with each proposal's receipt, and llm/. init --approvals writes review.approvals. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 not ok (review pending, contradictions, failing proofs or regressions, apply refused), 2 usage or error, 3 an LLM answer is needed. derive refuses while review is pending and, on contradictions, writes the returned decisions into the proposal.

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 not ok (review pending, contradictions, failing proofs or regressions, apply refused), 2 usage or error, 3 an LLM answer is needed. derive refuses while review is pending and, on contradictions, writes the returned decisions into the proposal.

useCases.name: Use Lastro from TypeScript, .NET or Go
useCases.before: Three SDKs expose the same pipeline (propose against the use cases, review with threads, pending, derive, returnDecisions, prove with the regression run, apply, gap review) with the same entities (use case, proposal, intent, proof), wire format, canonical hashes, seeded sampling, verdicts, receipts and prompts. Cross-check tests compare the .NET and Go reports and hashes with the TypeScript SDK, and all three with the Rust prover, on the reference login and its planted bugs.
useCases.after: Three SDKs expose the same pipeline (propose against the features, review with threads, pending, derive, returnDecisions, prove with the regression run, apply, gap review) with the same entities (feature, proposal, intent, proof), wire format, canonical hashes, seeded sampling, verdicts, receipts and prompts. Cross-check tests compare the .NET and Go reports and hashes with the TypeScript SDK, and all three with the Rust prover, on the reference login and its planted bugs. Every public type, function and field that said use case says feature, with no aliases.

useCases.name: Share one workspace across CLIs
useCases.before: The TypeScript, .NET and Go CLIs read and write the same .lastro/ files (config.json, usecases/, proof/, proposals/ and llm/), so one can propose, another review, and a third derive, prove and apply. A proposal approved by one SDK has a valid approval hash for the others, and proofs and baselines hash the same in all three.
useCases.after: The TypeScript, .NET and Go CLIs read and write the same .lastro/ files (config.json, features/, proof/, proposals/ and llm/), so one can propose, another review, and a third derive, prove and apply. A proposal approved by one SDK has a valid approval hash for the others, and proofs and baselines hash the same in all three.

useCases.name: Explore the pipeline in the sandbox
useCases.before: A web app (Vite, React, shadcn/ui) runs the real TypeScript SDK and the WASM prover on a store-login example with its own use cases. Under the pipeline gates, a feedback banner says what Lastro needs next and from whom: the team when review is pending or the spec contradicts itself (with a button that sends the contradictions back as decisions), whoever writes the code when proofs fail or a regression appears (the agent brief with counterexamples, copyable, with the same count as the Prove gate), or that every gate passes. useCases.name: Gate an agent's code edits on reviewed intents
useCases.before: The Lastro plugin for Claude Code and Codex (plugins/lastro) is active in a repository that has .lastro/plugin.json. Its PreToolUse hook treats the first attempt to edit source code, in any mode (plan mode, auto mode, an informal plan or none), as the moment to extract intents: edit tools (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, apply_patch) on code outside .lastro/ and outside the configured allow globs are denied, with steps to write the change as prose in .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.md, run lastro propose and start the user's review, unless the current proposal is approved, its proofs were derived from exactly its current intents and decisions, and its last proof run has not passed yet. Once every proof passes, the next source edit is a new change and is denied the same way. With gate "off" it never blocks. Proposals and handoff answers inside .lastro/ are always allowed; the proposal and use-case JSON files, receipts, config.json and the plugin's state are denied because only the CLI writes them; edits to .lastro/plugin.json ask the user in Claude Code and are denied in Codex. SessionStart adds the progress board and the rule that the agent is the author of the proposal and never approves it; UserPromptSubmit adds one short line (the board summary and that rule) only when the summary changed since the agent of that session last got it, and nothing otherwise.
useCases.after: The Lastro plugin for Claude Code and Codex (plugins/lastro) is active in a repository that has .lastro/plugin.json. Its PreToolUse hook treats the first attempt to edit source code, in any mode (plan mode, auto mode, an informal plan or none), as the moment to extract intents: edit tools (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, apply_patch) on code outside .lastro/ and outside the configured allow globs are denied, with steps to write the change as prose in .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.md, run lastro propose and start the user's review, unless the current proposal is approved, its proofs were derived from exactly its current intents and decisions, and its last proof run has not passed yet. SessionStart adds the progress board and the rule that the agent is the author of the proposal and never approves it; UserPromptSubmit adds one short line (the board summary and that rule) only when the summary changed since the agent of that session last got it, and nothing otherwise.

useCases.name: Prove the agent's implementation when it stops
useCases.before: With a derived proposal, the plugin's Stop hook runs the configured build command and lastro prove --stream with the configured arguments, appending the events to .lastro/plugin/progress.jsonl after a build event. Failing proofs or regressions in other use cases (or a failed build, recorded as a result event with its error) block the stop and return the failures and counterexamples to the agent as its next instruction, numbered against maxIterations (default 5) per proposal; after that the stop goes through and the user takes over. Passing proofs, or an unchanged code base whose last proof passed, end the turn. A code edit after a proof marks it stale in .lastro/plugin/state.json, so the next stop proves again.
useCases.after: With a derived proposal, the plugin's Stop hook runs the configured build command and lastro prove --stream with the configured arguments, appending the events to .lastro/plugin/progress.jsonl after a build event. Failing proofs or regressions in other features (or a failed build, recorded as a result event with its error) block the stop and return the failures and counterexamples to the agent as its next instruction, numbered against maxIterations (default 5) per proposal; after that the stop goes through and the user takes over. Passing proofs, or an unchanged code base whose last proof passed, end the turn. A code edit after a proof marks it stale in .lastro/plugin/state.json, so the next stop proves again.

useCases.name: Show the proposal's progress board
useCases.before: The plugin renders, from the CLI's status output and the files in .lastro/, a board for the current proposal with the stages (intents extracted, decisions answered, intents approved per the policy, proofs derived, verification), the existing proofs its intents replace, any regression in other use cases, and one line per proof: ✓ proved, ≈ evidenced, ✗ violated with its counterexample, ! weak or vacuous, ○ pending, plus the beyond-proof intents and the next step. It is shown to the user after every lastro command and on every stop, added to the agent's context on session start (later prompts get its one-line summary when it changes), and printed by lastro-plugin.mjs board (or one line with --line, for a status line); lastro-plugin.mjs prove builds, proves and prints it.
useCases.after: The plugin renders, from the CLI's status output and the files in .lastro/, a board for the current proposal with the stages (intents extracted, decisions answered, intents approved per the policy, proofs derived, verification), the existing proofs its intents replace, any regression in other features, and one line per proof: ✓ proved, ≈ evidenced, ✗ violated with its counterexample, ! weak or vacuous, ○ pending, plus the beyond-proof intents and the next step. It is shown to the user after every lastro command and on every stop, added to the agent's context on session start (later prompts get its one-line summary when it changes), and printed by lastro-plugin.mjs board (or one line with --line, for a status line); lastro-plugin.mjs prove builds, proves and prints it.

useCases.name: Stream a proof run as it happens
useCases.before: lastro prove --stream (TypeScript, Go and .NET CLIs) prints one compact JSON object per line instead of the single result: start (the proposal and the ids of the proofs it runs), progress every 100 runs of the code under proof, one proof event per proof, the proposal's own and every use case's regression proof alike (proof, role, verdict, passed, and the counterexample when there is one), crosscheck (enginesAgree) when the Rust prover ran, and result with the body prove prints without --stream. Exit codes and the files written are the same as without it. The Go and .NET tests compare their stream with the TypeScript CLI's on one workspace.
useCases.after: lastro prove --stream (TypeScript, Go and .NET CLIs) prints one compact JSON object per line instead of the single result: start (the proposal and the ids of the proofs it runs), progress every 100 runs of the code under proof, one proof event per proof, the proposal's own and every feature's regression proof alike (proof, role, verdict, passed, and the counterexample when there is one), crosscheck (enginesAgree) when the Rust prover ran, and result with the body prove prints without --stream. Exit codes and the files written are the same as without it. The Go and .NET tests compare their stream with the TypeScript CLI's on one workspace.

useCases.name: Show approvals and proofs live beside the chat
useCases.before: The lastro-board mod for Claude Code (plugins/lastro-board) reads .lastro/ once a second when the session starts in a repository with a Lastro workspace: config, the current proposal, the use cases and the plugin's progress.jsonl. It opens a pane with the review (each decision answered or not, each intent with its approvals out of the policy's count and the proofs it replaces) and the proofs (○ pending, … running, ✓ proved, ≈ evidenced, ✗ violated with its counterexample, ! weak or vacuous, and the beyond-proof intents), updating each proof as the run under way reports it. It shows a one-line summary above the prompt and in the status line, and a toast when every intent is approved and when a proof run ends. /lastro-board opens the pane. It decides nothing and works only in Claude Code.
useCases.after: The lastro-board mod for Claude Code (plugins/lastro-board) reads .lastro/ once a second when the session starts in a repository with a Lastro workspace: config, the current proposal, the features and the plugin's progress.jsonl. It opens a pane with the review (each decision answered or not, each intent with its approvals out of the policy's count and the proofs it replaces) and the proofs (○ pending, … running, ✓ proved, ≈ evidenced, ✗ violated with its counterexample, ! weak or vacuous, and the beyond-proof intents), updating each proof as the run under way reports it. It shows a one-line summary above the prompt and in the status line, and a toast when every intent is approved and when a proof run ends. /lastro-board opens the pane. It decides nothing and works only in Claude Code.

useCases.name: Store features and proposals
useCases.before: The workspace keeps one file per entity: each use case in .lastro/usecases/<id>-<slug>.json (id, slug, name, description, history), each proof of a use case in .lastro/proof/<proof-id>-<slug>.json and each proposal in .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.json, with its receipt next to it. Use cases are numbered UC-001, UC-002... and proposals P-001, P-002... with the next free number, never reused even after a removal; intents and proofs are numbered inside their proposal (P-007.I-03, P-007.PF-05) and keep that id when a proof moves to its use case; proofs derived straight from a use case are numbered inside it (UC-003.PF-01). Slugs are kebab-case and stable: a rename changes only the name. intents.json, spec.json and proof.json are no longer written. A use case file that still carries a proofs list is read as before, and its proofs move to .lastro/proof/ the next time the workspace writes that use case.
useCases.after: The workspace keeps one file per entity: each feature in .lastro/features/<id>-<slug>.json (id, slug, name, description, history), each proof of a feature in .lastro/proof/<proof-id>-<slug>.json and each proposal in .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.json, with its receipt next to it. Features are numbered F-001, F-002... and proposals P-001, P-002... with the next free number, never reused even after a removal; intents and proofs are numbered inside their proposal (P-007.I-03, P-007.PF-05) and keep that id when a proof moves to its feature; proofs derived straight from a feature are numbered inside it (F-003.PF-01). Slugs are kebab-case and stable: a rename changes only the name. intents.json, spec.json and proof.json are no longer written. A feature file that still carries a proofs list is read as before, and its proofs move to .lastro/proof/ the next time the workspace writes that feature.

useCases.name: Track a proposal's status
useCases.before: A proposal has one status: open while its review is pending; changes-requested while a reviewer has an open thread; approved once approval succeeds; proving once its proofs are derived; proved when every proof, new and regression, passes; applied once apply has synced the use cases; closed when it is abandoned. status lists the proposals with their status, and status <proposal> its pending items.
useCases.after: A proposal has one status: open while its review is pending; changes-requested while a reviewer has an open thread; approved once approval succeeds; proving once its proofs are derived; proved when every proof, new and regression, passes; applied once apply has synced the features; closed when it is abandoned. status lists the proposals with their status, and status <proposal> its pending items.

useCases.name: Keep proofs as regression tests
useCases.before: A proof that passed belongs to its use case, stored in its own file, .lastro/proof/<proof-id>-<slug>.json, with its id, slug, name, description, use case, model, subject, check, status and verdict, and the intent and proposal it came from when it came from one; the workspace finds a use case's proofs by their useCase field. Only passed proofs run as regression tests; a pending or failed proof derived from a use case does not. prove(proposal) runs the proposal's pending proofs and the proofs of every use case except the ones the proposal supersedes, so a change that breaks any use case fails as a regression, on a touched use case or not; a superseded proof that still passes is noted, since the behavior may not have changed; failures go back to the implementer through feedback. lastro regress runs every use case's proofs alone, for example in CI. A use case with no proofs yet is reported as unproved rather than failing.
useCases.after: A proof that passed belongs to its feature, stored in its own file, .lastro/proof/<proof-id>-<slug>.json, with its id, slug, name, description, feature, model, subject, check, status and verdict, and the intent and proposal it came from when it came from one; the workspace finds a feature's proofs by their feature field. Only passed proofs run as regression tests; a pending or failed proof derived from a feature does not. prove(proposal) runs the proposal's pending proofs and the proofs of every feature except the ones the proposal supersedes, so a change that breaks any feature fails as a regression, on a touched feature or not; a superseded proof that still passes is noted, since the behavior may not have changed; failures go back to the implementer through feedback. lastro regress runs every feature's proofs alone, for example in CI. A feature with no proofs yet is reported as unproved rather than failing.

useCases.name: Apply a proposal
useCases.before: apply(proposal), in the library and as lastro apply <proposal>, refuses unless the proposal is approved, unchanged since approval, has no open decision, and every proof, new and regression, passes. It then writes each resulting use case (adds the use case file, replaces the description and name, or deletes the file of a removed use case), writes each passing proof to .lastro/proof/ as a regression test of its use case, deletes the files of the superseded proofs, appends the proposal id to each touched use case's history, records the new baseline hash in the receipt and sets the proposal's status to applied.
useCases.after: apply(proposal), in the library and as lastro apply <proposal>, refuses unless the proposal is approved, unchanged since approval, has no open decision, and every proof, new and regression, passes. It then writes each resulting feature (adds the feature file, replaces the description and name, or deletes the file of a removed feature), writes each passing proof to .lastro/proof/ as a regression test of its feature, deletes the files of the superseded proofs, appends the proposal id to each touched feature's history, records the new baseline hash in the receipt and sets the proposal's status to applied.

useCases.name: Derive proofs from the established features
useCases.before: lastro derive --usecases derives proofs straight from the established use cases, with no proposal and no intents: by default for every use case that has no proofs, or for the ids it is given (--usecases UC-003,UC-016). The derive step reads each use case's description, the models and subjects declared in .lastro/config.json and the proofs other use cases already have, and writes pending proofs numbered inside their use case (UC-003.PF-01) to .lastro/proof/. A use case the models cannot express gets no proof and is listed as unprovable with the reason. A use case that already has proofs is refused: its proofs change only through a proposal. lastro prove --usecases runs the pending proofs of the use cases together with every passed proof. A pending proof that passes becomes passed and from then on runs as a regression test, in prove and in lastro regress. A pending proof that fails stays failed and is reported with the note that the code is the reference: either the description is wrong, and a proposal fixes it, or the code has a bug the user decides about; it never goes back to the code as feedback.
useCases.after: lastro derive --features derives proofs straight from the established features, with no proposal and no intents: by default for every feature that has no proofs, or for the ids it is given (--features F-003,F-016). The derive step reads each feature's description, the models and subjects declared in .lastro/config.json and the proofs other features already have, and writes pending proofs numbered inside their feature (F-003.PF-01) to .lastro/proof/. A feature the models cannot express gets no proof and is listed as unprovable with the reason. A feature that already has proofs is refused: its proofs change only through a proposal. lastro prove --features runs the pending proofs of the features together with every passed proof. A pending proof that passes becomes passed and from then on runs as a regression test, in prove and in lastro regress. A pending proof that fails stays failed and is reported with the note that the code is the reference: either the description is wrong, and a proposal fixes it, or the code has a bug the user decides about; it never goes back to the code as feedback. There is no --usecases option.

decisions.name: How long old names live
decisions.question: How long do --usecases and the old SDK names keep working?

options.label: One release, with a notice
options.consequence: Callers get a release to move; then the aliases are removed.

options.label: Remove now
options.consequence: Cleaner, but every script and integration that uses the old names breaks at once.

decisions.name: Rename the ids too
decisions.question: Should the ids change from UC-003 to F-003, or keep UC- and rename only the word?

options.label: F- ids, migrated on next write
options.consequence: Consistent naming everywhere; every file, proof id and hash is rewritten once, old ids stay in history.

options.label: Keep UC- ids
options.consequence: No file or proof id churn, but the id says use case while everything else says feature.
